subject: System Design
title: Circuit Breakers
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Circuit Breakers.

hook.text: A downstream service is down. Your service keeps calling it, waiting for timeouts. Every request takes 30s and fails.

buildup.text: A circuit breaker monitors failures. After a threshold of consecutive failures, it opens — blocking all calls instantly.

discovery.text: When open, calls fail instantly without waiting. After a cooldown, one test request checks if the service recovered.

twist.text: Without circuit breakers, a slow dependency slows your service too. With them, you fail fast and gracefully degrade.

climax.text: Circuit breakers prevent cascading failures by isolating unhealthy dependencies and failing fast instead of waiting.

punchline.text: Fail fast when a dependency is down — don't wait and suffer.

quiz.question: What does an open circuit breaker do?
options: Blocks all calls to the failing service and returns errors immediately
Routes traffic to a different service
